reviewNotes: Hosted in the home's own media folder on its website vendor's storage, so provenance is posted. The printed date, August 8, 2024, is 25 months before retrieval, so the loader holds it until the home confirms it is still current.
The PDF is a 16-page scan with no text layer; the text field is a transcription of the itemized lines on pages 1 and 5-12, read page by page.
Visitation, funeral ceremony and graveside service are priced per hour ($250); each is recorded as that benchmark's observation with the unit in its name.

Direct cremation: the Direct Cremation Package with the minimum alternative container ($2,700) is the observation. It includes an urn and one certified death certificate, and excludes the medical examiner's cremation approval stamp.
Death certificates: the Maryland first-copy price ($25) is the observation for this Maryland home; DC and Virginia copies are for deaths there.
Holding remains after a 7-day grace period ($35 per day) is the per-day shelter fee.

Private-viewing add-ons, security, limousine overtime, per-card acknowledgement cards, the mock casket and the single doeskin casket are kept off their benchmarks. Packages, youth services and immediate burial have no benchmark. Caskets, urns, vaults, flowers, programs and the cremation fee are ranges and never enter the benchmark feed.

This review found eight matcher gaps on real Maryland wording, fixed in lib/negotiation/price-list-parse.ts: the direct-cremation package read as a cremation container, the basic service fee and funeral ceremony matched nothing, wood caskets read as metal, and urn or casket personalization read as the urn or casket.
